content.user_title: Build Android Compose UIs with Expert Guidance
content.value_statement: Modern Android teams need Compose guidance that avoids fragile state and navigation patterns. This skill provides practical patterns for state, navigation, performance, and Material 3.
actual_capabilities: Explains Compose project setup with BOM and common UI dependencies.
Shows ViewModel and StateFlow patterns for predictable UI state.
Demonstrates screen and content composable separation with callbacks.
Covers type-safe Navigation Compose routes and destination handling.
Lists performance practices for recomposition, stability, and remembered work.
Provides troubleshooting guidance for infinite recomposition loops.
limitations: Does not run Gradle, Android Studio, or device tests for the user.
Uses short examples, not a complete production app template.
Dependency versions in the guide may need updates for newer projects.
Focuses on Compose and does not deeply cover legacy XML views.

use_cases.title: Plan a New Compose App
use_cases.description: Create a baseline architecture for a new Android app using Compose, ViewModel, StateFlow, and Material 3.
use_cases.target_user: Android developers starting a greenfield project

use_cases.title: Refactor UI State Handling
use_cases.description: Move screen state into clear ViewModel flows and pass only state and callbacks into child composables.

use_cases.title: Improve Compose Performance
use_cases.description: Find recomposition risks, unstable UI models, and expensive work inside composable functions.
use_cases.target_user: Teams tuning an existing Compose codebase

prompt_templates.title: Create a Compose Screen
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design a Jetpack Compose screen for [feature]. Include UI state, loading, error, and success states.

prompt_templates.title: Set Up State Management
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a ViewModel and StateFlow pattern for [screen]. Explain the state fields, events, and composable boundaries.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Type-Safe Navigation
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a type-safe Navigation Compose structure for [app flow]. Include route models, arguments, and screen responsibilities.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose Recomposition Problems
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Compose UI behavior: [describe issue]. Identify likely recomposition causes and suggest stable state and remember strategies.

output_examples.input: I need a profile screen with loading, error, and loaded states.
output: A recommended UI state model with separate loading, error, and data fields.
A screen composable that reads state from a ViewModel.
A content composable that receives state and retry callbacks.

output_examples.input: My Compose list recomposes too often when filters change.
output: A checklist for unstable parameters, new object creation, and expensive work in composition.
Suggested use of remembered derived state for calculated values.
Guidance to move sorting and filtering out of the composable body.

output_examples.input: I want type-safe navigation from Home to Profile with a user identifier.
output: A route model plan for Home and Profile destinations.
A navigation flow that passes the user identifier as typed route data.
Screen responsibility notes that keep navigation at the screen boundary.

best_practices: Provide the target screen, state requirements, and navigation flow before asking for architecture guidance.
Ask for state hoisting and callback boundaries when designing reusable composables.
Review dependency versions against the current Android documentation before implementation.
anti_patterns: Do not ask the skill to execute build commands or verify runtime behavior.
Do not pass complete app ownership to one composable without separating screen and content roles.
Do not copy dependency versions without checking compatibility with the project setup.

faq.question: Does this skill generate complete Android projects?
faq.answer: No. It provides patterns and examples for Compose architecture, state, navigation, and performance.

faq.question: Can it help migrate XML layouts to Compose?
faq.answer: Yes. It can guide screen decomposition, state ownership, and replacement of view-based UI patterns.

faq.question: Does it support Material Design 3?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes Material 3 dependency guidance and Compose UI structure advice.

faq.question: Can it diagnose recomposition issues?
faq.answer: Yes. It can suggest checks for unstable data, expensive composition work, and missing remember usage.

faq.question: Does it require network access?
faq.answer: No. The skill is documentation-only and does not require network calls or external commands.
